_doc: Reviewed exceptions for devtools/hygiene_check.py (fix wave 25, founder ruling R-HYGIENE). 'allow': static-lint exceptions — rule, path, optional function, optional 'contains' (a snippet of the flagged line), and a mandatory reason; `lint --strict-allowlist` (CI) fails an entry that matches nothing. 'expected_skips': per suite id, the skip reasons that are legitimate on some machine (regex over the reason pytest/go/cargo/node reports); any other skip fails the run (rule R5). Add an entry only with a reason a reviewer can check. 'platform_only_tests': per suite id, every test that exists on some OSes only — 'test' (its name as the runner prints it: cargo's `test <name> ...`, go's top-level `=== RUN <name>`), 'only_on' (sys.platform names, 'linux' for Linux) and 'why'. docs/test-counts.md counts every test and names these in its last column (`counts --check` fails if the column and this list differ); on another OS R6 expects exactly these tests absent by name and the count lower by that many, and fails if a listed test runs where it should not or is missing where it should run (fix wave 26a, W26-5: replaced 'count_os_delta', an anonymous per-OS number).

allow.reason: Guards against a retry/backoff loop when the ledger is down (the alternative is waiting out the 10 s upstream client timeout). The measured path is one refused loopback connect plus a 502 written by an in-process httptest server — no CPU-bound work, milliseconds — so 2 s is a >100x margin, and the structural half of the property (zero detection calls) is asserted separately. Reviewed fix wave 25 (E-C).

Separates two causes of the close: answered-and-closed at once (correct) vs closed by the 5 s body deadline (the regression: the server waited for the body). The bound is the server's own deadline (const = server.rs BODY_READ_TIMEOUT), measured from before the request was sent and read right after the 401, so only the 401 + close itself (no CPU-bound work) is inside it. Reviewed fix wave 25 (E-C).

Ordering, not speed: the slow reader can only be cut by the 15 s request deadline, which starts after `since`; others answered before since + 15 s were answered before the cut, which a server serialising them behind the slow reader cannot do. Bound = the server's own deadline (const = server.rs REQUEST_DEADLINE); the work inside it is one /health and one append. Reviewed fix wave 25 (E-C).
